column3: Directly pairs following conjecture with lack of knowledge and its failure before truth.
Adds a boundary between belief and doubt without establishing the focus claim.
Shows plural conjectures can sustain divergent readings under pressure.
Shows majority-following built on conjecture and estimation can mislead.
Frames the surrounding contrast between divine origination and rival claims.
Shows a conjecture becoming socially confirmed through followers' own adherence.
Applies following conjecture to claims about associates, but repeats the core warning.
Supplies the immediate contrast: guidance to truth versus a guide needing guidance.
Preserves a reading where zan is a serious, action-shaping expectation, not bare guesswork.
Links widespread belief with association, but does not clarify zan or truth.
Shows fear can resist following guidance; its conjectural route is only channel-level.
Marks truth as a disclosed source and preserves the consequence of choosing against it.
Connects following conjecture with inherited names, desire, absent authority, and received guidance.
Contrasts conduct without truth, but does not address conjecture's epistemic role.
Questions deficient assumptions about the Lord while leaving a stronger reading possible.
Contrasts the true divine promise with the majority's lack of knowledge.
Adds divine words' stability, but is indirect for conjecture versus truth.
Contrasts demanded knowledge with following conjecture and fabricating judgments.
Shows a stated certainty being reduced to conjecture and non-certainty.
Presents guidance and the religion of truth as publicly attested, through a parallel channel.
Makes following a differentiator between falsehood and truth from the Lord.
Uses majority ignorance in a different question of guardianship.
Challenges unauthorized classifications attributed to God in the same local argument.
Shows a conjectural assumption giving way to recognition when imagined supports vanish.
Contrasts creaturely knowledge of devotion with divine knowledge of deeds only indirectly.
Offers a positive criterion for following: unguided by payment and themselves guided.
Identifies a purposeless-world assumption as a disbelieving conjecture.
Parallels the claim that a supposed protector will not avail anything.
The nearby channel is not localized to this ayah's wording.
Shows harmful conjecture about the Lord as an action-shaping cause of ruin.
No material addition to conjecture, truth, following, or knowledge.
Judgment and mercy are relevant only through an unlocalized secondary channel.
Preserves a reading of zan as an action-governing expectation of return.
Speaks of sectarian division and later disclosure, not the focus relation.
Links created measures, truth, and knowing, without treating conjecture.
Names followers of the Prophet but supplies no epistemic contrast.
Parallels the failure of a person's contrivance to avail anything.
Places deeds under just recompense and divine accounting, indirectly supporting the closing clause.
Affirms God's true authority when other supports fail.
Restates divine knowledge of deeds without the conjecture-truth contrast.
The same surah's divine witnessing of every deed supports the final knowledge clause.
Shows a formerly trusted assumption being reclassified after contrary evidence.
Contrasts loss of knowledge with God's complete knowledge.
Shows following a leader whose command lacks sound judgment.
Provides following the messenger as a route toward guidance, not an automatic equivalence.
Differentiates kinds of conjecture and warns against harmful suspicion.

Preserves a reading in which zan can be supported by signs and become settled recognition.
Uses majority ignorance in response to an accusation, without the focus structure.
Contrasts following what was sent down with following other protectors.
Contrasts knowledgeable recognition of the Hour's truth with disputation.
No clear addition beyond a limit placed on future belief.
Contrasts ordered repair with following the path of corrupters.
Shows shared repetition of an assumption does not create independent evidence.
Parallels that a precaution cannot avail against God, while preserving Jacob's knowledge.
Depicts fruitless deeds but has no clear conjecture or truth relation.
Links lack of scriptural knowledge with wishes and conjecture.
Shows following as an incremental path into wrongdoing.
No localized addition to the focus claim.
Treats resurrection expectation as required by signs, rather than excusing uncertainty.
Uses conditional assessment within a legal decision, not the focus's epistemic contrast.
Links judging by truth with being guided to a straight middle path.
Shows zan approaching compelled recognition under overwhelming evidence.
Names an untrue, ignorant conjecture about God and contrasts it with divine knowledge.
Exemplifies a call to follow messengers through embodied, purposeful movement.
Affirms the Lord's word becoming due, but is too indirect.
Parallels the failure of acquired things and protectors to avail anything.
Contrasts denial of arriving truth with a later disclosure of consequences.
Shows zan hardening from fear into recognition through accumulating signs.
Demands proof for rival gods and diagnoses turning away from truth through ignorance.
Divine mastery is only a remote contextual support.
Explicitly sets truth from the Lord against doubt.
Following is tested here, but its evidence relation is indirect.
States an undoubted gathering and contrasts it with self-loss and unbelief.
Shows zan becoming recognition of an unavoidable separation.
Provides a concrete record-and-witness practice ordered toward justice and avoiding doubt.
Contrasts close recognition with refusal to believe, through a parallel channel.
Following a means in travel does not clarify the focus claim.
The immediate passage challenges fabricated claims about God and their assumed impunity.
No material addition to the focus's epistemic contrast.
Pairs arguing without knowledge with following every rebellious devil.
Divine knowledge of the mindful is too general to add to the focus.
Shows how a community should receive an unproven report without spreading suspicion.
Only lexically echoes not availing, in an unrelated image.
Sets clear evidence, a witness, and prior scripture against doubt, naming truth from the Lord.
Only repeats not availing in a different physical context.
Directly joins lack of knowledge with being nothing but conjecturers.
Directly rejects a theological claim as knowledge-less estimation.
Defines following as constrained by revelation, with limited relation to the focus.
Shows repeated signs and correction after denial, without explicitly treating conjecture.

Calls believers true, but offers no account of conjecture or knowledge.

Contrasts emphatic denial with God's binding true promise and widespread ignorance.
Mocks messengers but does not clarify the focus relation.
Contrasts unsupported human saying with God's true speech and guiding path.

Pairs speaking only truth about God with an explicit proof.
Creation stages do not materially clarify conjecture, following, or truth here.
Shows listening being used to construct a false label that others are then asked to follow.
Contrasts inherited following with following what God sent down and with reasoned guidance.
Warns against pursuing ambiguous material for discord instead of its grounded interpretation.
Directly contrasts lack of knowledge and following conjecture with certainty.
Forbids following desires of people who went astray and misled many.
Challenges inherited practice when it lacks knowledge or guidance.
Rejects following desire in place of revealed direction and warns that it misleads.
Contrasts seeking other judgment with a Book detailed in truth.
Forbids following the desires of those who deny signs and do not believe in the hereafter.
Sets following God's straight path against dispersing alternative paths.
Challenges an inherited claim about God that lacks divine authorization.
Links following the messenger with guidance and success.
Shows following desire as a route away from signs and toward error.
Defines the messenger and his followers as calling upon clear insight.
Directs those without knowledge to ask those who possess remembrance.

Forbids obeying one who follows desire and neglects remembrance.

Makes following divine guidance the contrast to going astray or falling into hardship.
Shows that truth cannot be measured by the desires of the many.
Exposes taking desire as a god as a rival to guidance.
Calls following desire without guidance from God the deepest form of error.
Pairs following desires without knowledge with injustice and lack of a guide.

Sets a revealed way against following the desires of those who do not know.

Contrasts following what pleases God with following one's own desires.

Contrasts speech from desire with speech governed by revelation.
